coreMechanic.notes: Breath-controlled flight is unique, physically embodied, and produces genuine behavioral signal. Skill expression via breath variance and spike avoidance. Touch fallback ensures inclusivity.

instantDelight.notes: Sky gradient + coin particles + trail effect create beautiful visuals. Near-miss messages, streak badge, score pop all provide immediate feedback.

signalQuality.notes: 4 genuine behavioral signals captured: breathVariance, avgAltitude, coinsCollected, spikeCollisions. 5 deterministic personality archetypes with meaningful conditions.

polish.notes: Framer-motion transitions, pulse rings, coin particles, float texts, streak badge, near-miss overlay, 'New Best!' banner. Very polished execution.

technicalQuality.notes: Zero TypeScript 'as any' casts. No setState in RAF loop. Proper cleanup (cancelAnimationFrame, clearInterval, stopMusic, stream.getTracks().stop). All 24 Playwright tests pass.

brandFit.notes: Universal appeal, calming/positive emotional valence. Customizable via brand theme URL param. Creates positive brand association through relaxing play.

accessibility.notes: Touch fallback for no-mic environments. axe-core passes (no critical/serious violations). No horizontal scroll on iPhone SE/15 Pro Max. End screen fits iPhone SE viewport.

creativDirectorNotes: Breath Rider is one of the strongest Glimmers in the library. The core mechanic — blowing into the mic to make a rider climb — is physically embodied, universally accessible, and produces genuine emotional/behavioral signal. The sky gradient with coin sparkle particles and a trail effect creates a beautiful visual experience. The 45-second duration is perfectly calibrated for brand activations: long enough to collect meaningful signal, short enough for repeat play. The 5 personality archetypes (Steady, Guardian, Sage, Nurturer, Harmonizer) are thoughtful and cover the behavioral space well. The progressive difficulty ramp (1.5x → 3.2x scroll speed) ensures both casual and competitive players find appropriate challenge. The touch fallback is essential for accessibility. Minor areas for future polish: hapticWarning on timer countdown, and potentially a visual indicator showing breath strength in real-time.
